title: Kohli Is Worth ₹3,542 Crore. Shah Rukh Khan Is Second.
excerpt: The first Fortune India-Interbrand celebrity ranking puts a cricketer at the top. Three of the top ten are from cricket. The other seven are from Bollywood.
body:
# Kohli Is Worth ₹3,542 Crore. Shah Rukh Khan Is Second.

The inaugural Fortune India-Interbrand Celebrity Brand Value Study has placed Virat Kohli at the top of its rankings with a brand valuation of ₹3,542 crore — roughly $420 million. He is ahead of Shah Rukh Khan in second and Priyanka Chopra Jonas in third. It is the first time a study of this kind has been conducted in India, and a cricketer has beaten every film star in the country.

The ranking measured celebrity brands across six dimensions: distinctiveness, engagement, trust, affinity, coherence, and responsibility. It went beyond salary and endorsement deals to assess the institutional weight of a celebrity's name. On every metric, Kohli came out on top.

## Cricket's Dominance

Three cricketers made the top ten. After Kohli, MS Dhoni ranked fourth — years after retiring from international cricket, his brand endures in a way that defies the usual shelf life of an athlete's commercial relevance. Sachin Tendulkar, who retired from all cricket in 2013, placed eighth. The fact that a retired cricketer can still outrank active Bollywood stars tells you something about what cricket means in India.

The remaining seven spots went to film industry figures. The 7:3 split between Bollywood and cricket in the top ten mirrors the two pillars of Indian popular culture — entertainment and sport — but the top slot going to a cricketer marks a shift in the hierarchy.

## The Business of Being Kohli

Kohli's commercial infrastructure is vast. He commands 271 million followers on Instagram alone — more than any other cricketer in history and more than most Bollywood stars. A single sponsored post on his feed costs an estimated ₹14 crore. His endorsement portfolio includes Myntra, PUMA, Hero MotoCorp, MRF Tyres, American Tourister, and several others.

But the ranking suggests his value goes beyond endorsement volume. The Fortune India-Interbrand methodology specifically measured **trust** and **coherence** — how consistently a celebrity's public persona aligns with the brands they represent. Kohli's well-publicised decision, made years ago, to only endorse products he personally uses appears to have paid dividends in credibility.

He is also expanding beyond endorsements. His lifestyle brand One8 — which spans fragrances, restaurants, and sportswear — is preparing a new footwear line where Kohli enters as co-founder rather than ambassador. The distinction matters: it marks a transition from lending his name to building equity in his own ventures.

## What This Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs, Kohli's brand value is not an abstract number. It reflects the purchasing power and cultural influence of the diaspora market. When PUMA signs Kohli, it is not just buying access to Indian consumers in Mumbai and Delhi. It is buying access to Indian consumers in London, Toronto, the Bay Area, and Dubai. The brands that invest in Kohli are, by extension, investing in the global Indian consumer.

The fact that three cricketers — and specifically these three cricketers, each of whom is a household name in every Indian home worldwide — dominate the ranking underscores a simple reality. For the Indian diaspora, cricket is not just a sport. It is a shared cultural shorthand, a way of staying connected to home regardless of which country you live in. Kohli's influence extends beyond sports; it impacts remittances and tourism as fans are more likely to travel back to India for cricket events, further strengthening ties to their homeland.

## The RCB Factor

The ranking comes weeks after Kohli's Royal Challengers Bengaluru won a second consecutive IPL title. Despite being ruled out of the upcoming Afghanistan ODI series with a hamstring injury, his visibility has only increased. The IPL final drew massive viewership, and Kohli's celebration — widely shared across social media — became one of the most engaged-with posts in Indian sports history.

At 37, Kohli is no longer at the peak of his athletic career. His Test average has dipped. His body breaks down more often. But the Fortune India-Interbrand ranking suggests that his cultural relevance has, if anything, accelerated. The brand has outrun the batting average, and the gap is only widening.

Rohit Sharma, by comparison, commands a social media fee of approximately ₹75 lakhs per sponsored post — significant, but less than six percent of what Kohli charges. Dhoni, despite his continued commercial pull, sits behind three Bollywood names in the ranking. The distance between Kohli and every other Indian athlete is not a gap. It is a gulf.
